prompt:
Find real, documented post-mortems of major cloud outages in 2025 (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud or Cloudflare). For each, cite the provider's own incident report and quote what it says the root cause was.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are documented post-mortems for major cloud outages in 2025, based on the provider's own incident reports. 

**1. Cloudflare Outage on November 18, 2025**
Cloudflare experienced a widespread network outage caused by a database permissions change that broke their Bot Management system's feature file distribution.
SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/18-november-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Instead, it was triggered by a change to one of our database systems' permissions which caused the database to output multiple entries into a “feature file” used by our Bot Management system." | CLAIM: The root cause of the Nov 18 Cloudflare outage was a database permissions change that corrupted a feature file.
SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/18-november-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "That feature file, in turn, doubled in size. The larger-than-expected feature file was then propagated to all the machines that make up our network." | CLAIM: The corrupted feature file doubled in size, which caused network routing software to fail when it propagated.

**2. AWS DynamoDB Service Disruption on October 19-20, 2025**
Amazon Web Services experienced a major disruption to DynamoDB in the us-east-1 region due to a DNS management race condition.
SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/aws--2025-10-19--dynamodb-dns-service-disruption-us-east-1/ | QUOTE: "The incident stemmed from a latent race condition in the DynamoDB DNS management system that resulted in an incorrect empty DNS record for the service’s regional endpoint." | CLAIM: The root cause of the Oct 19-20 AWS DynamoDB outage was a race condition in the DNS management system that deleted IP addresses.
SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/aws--2025-10-19--dynamodb-dns-service-disruption-us-east-1/ | QUOTE: "The race condition occurred when a delayed DNS Enactor applied an outdated plan that overwrote a newer plan, and the cleanup process then deleted the old plan, removing all IP addresses for the regional endpoint." | CLAIM: The race condition mechanism involved a delayed enactor applying an outdated plan that overwrote a newer one, followed by a cleanup process that deleted all endpoint IP addresses.

**3. Microsoft Azure Front Door Outage on October 29-30, 2025**
Microsoft Azure suffered an 8.5-hour global outage across Azure Front Door and Azure CDN, taking down portals and Microsoft 365 services.
SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | QUOTE: "A specific sequence of customer configuration changes, performed across two different control plane build versions, resulted in incompatible customer configuration metadata being generated." | CLAIM: The trigger for the Azure Front Door outage was incompatible customer configuration metadata generated across different control plane builds.
SOURCE: https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | QUOTE: "These customer configuration changes themselves were valid and non-malicious – however they produced metadata that, when deployed to edge site servers, exposed a latent bug in the data plane." | CLAIM: The valid configuration changes exposed a latent data plane bug when deployed, which caused edge site crashes and DNS resolution errors.

**4. Cloudflare Dashboard and API Outage on September 12, 2025**
Cloudflare's dashboard and broad API services went down due to a bug causing infinite API calls that overwhelmed the Tenant Service.
SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage/ | QUOTE: "The incident’s impact stemmed from several issues, but the immediate trigger was a bug in the dashboard." | CLAIM: The root cause of the Sept 12 Cloudflare dashboard outage was a bug in the dashboard code.
SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage/ | QUOTE: "Because this object was recreated on every state or prop change, React treated it as “always new,” causing the useEffect to re-run each time. As a result, the API call executed many times during a single dashboard render instead of just once." | CLAIM: A React useEffect hook dependency bug caused the dashboard to make repeated, unnecessary API calls, which overwhelmed the service.

**5. Cloudflare Partial Outage on December 5, 2025**
A subset of Cloudflare's customers representing 28% of HTTP traffic received 500 errors due to a proxy bug triggered while responding to an industry-wide vulnerability.
SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Instead, it was triggered by changes being made to our body parsing logic while attempting to detect and mitigate an industry-wide vulnerability disclosed this week in React Server Components." | CLAIM: The root cause of the Dec 5 Cloudflare outage was changes made to body parsing logic during vulnerability mitigation.
SOURCE: https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | QUOTE: "Unfortunately, in our FL1 version of our proxy, under certain circumstances, the second change of turning off our WAF rule testing tool caused an error state that resulted in 500 HTTP error codes to be served from our network." | CLAIM: The proxy bug was specifically triggered by turning off the WAF rule testing tool under certain circumstances, causing 500 HTTP errors.
